common_name: Stewart's Solomon's Seal (Scrambling Whorled-Leaf Solomon's Seal)

planting.note: Plant rhizome divisions in spring or fall in humus-rich, moist, well-drained woodland soil in dappled to full shade; give it something low to scramble through, since the wiry stems lean and weave rather than stand upright.

directions: Plant divisions in humus-rich, consistently moist, well-drained soil in dappled or full shade, ideally with a low neighboring shrub or groundcover for the lax stems to lean against as they scramble outward. This rare Chinese woodlander from Sichuan and Yunnan differs sharply from the familiar arching border Solomon's seals: its whorled leaves ring the wiry stems in tiers rather than alternating in two flat rows, and its pinch-waisted, bottle-green-tipped flowers are speckled with tiny pink-purple dots before opening to reveal creamy throats, followed by red berries in autumn. It is slower to establish and less vigorous than mainstream garden Solomon's seals, rewarding patience with an unusual textural presence in a shaded rock garden or woodland trough where its scrambling habit can be appreciated up close. Keep soil evenly moist through summer and mulch with leaf litter to mimic its native forest floor.
sources: Plants of the World Online (Kew Science)

common_name: Byakko Solomon's Seal (White Tiger Variegated Solomon's Seal)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or fall in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in light to half shade; stable variegation can take a couple of seasons to fully develop on newly settled plants.

directions: Plant in humus-rich, evenly moist, well-drained soil in light to half shade, favoring a cool, dappled woodland site over deep, dry shade. Byakko, meaning 'white tiger,' is a once-nearly-extinct old Japanese cut-foliage selection reintroduced to cultivation by plantsman Barry Yinger; its glossy leaves emerge solid green and then develop a bold creamy-white half nearest the bright red stem, giving each leaf a distinctive two-toned, striped appearance that is bolder than plain-margined variegated forms. Small white, green-tipped bells hang beneath the arching stems in late spring. It is a reasonably vigorous grower for how heavily variegated it is, tolerates dry shade once established, and makes an eye-catching accent or cut-foliage plant in a woodland border.

common_name: Weihenstephan Solomon's Seal (Robust Tall Garden Solomon's Seal)

planting.note: Plant rhizome divisions in spring or fall in fertile, humus-rich, moist but well-drained soil in partial to full shade; give it extra room compared with dwarf Solomon's seal cultivars, since it builds into a notably tall, wide-arching clump.

directions: Plant divisions in fertile, humus-rich soil that stays evenly moist but drains well, siting in partial to full shade or a spot with only gentle morning sun. Weihenstephan is a robust, plain-green garden Solomon's seal selected for its unusually tall, dramatically arching stems, which carry ranks of glossy elliptic leaves well above most other Solomon's seal cultivars and can reach a yard or taller in good conditions. Small whitish, green-tipped bells dangle in neat rows beneath the foliage in late spring, followed by dark berries, and the clump spreads steadily by rhizome into a broad architectural colony. Its height and vigor make it a strong back-of-border choice for a shaded woodland or streamside planting, where it pairs well with hostas, ferns, and other coarse-textured shade companions; watch for slugs and the Solomon's seal sawfly, whose larvae can quickly skeletonize the foliage.
